stages.notes: Rule 11 and rule 9: a pull-started lift. Its link (UNHOOK/HOOK a rope shackle onto an eye) repeats AS-006 A/B, I, K and M. The prop pin is a carryable Load (add_pin, band_plate_shop.cpp:119-133), but it sits up on the 374 ring, out of reach from the plate. Body order: G's kit bodies are created in this order: the platform (154), tower (185), pin (202), handle (206) and shackle (216). They come after the upper-frame static body (484) and before H, I, the route body and the shop's frame body (486-491). The whole shop is built after the well and wet bands and before the crane, service and stack bands, the slingshot, swing, C6 and vertical machines (physics_world.cpp:220-264). Adding or removing any kit body here shifts the kit index and Jolt BodyID of every later kit body, and breaks old saves (physics_world_state.cpp:401-408 only tolerates bodies appended at the end). world_solids.inc is built before the player (physics_world.cpp:191), so kit changes do not reorder it. Ways to stay order-neutral, as this codebase already does: reuse G's existing body slots, or change parts only inside the static compound bodies (shop frame 1007, route 1008, upper frame), which adds no bodies, or build new bodies last (the physics_world.cpp:236-264 pattern).

stages.how_it_starts_now:
Picking up the spool and setting it down both links and starts the stage. Nothing is pulled.

Touch steps:
1. Walk with the stick to the spool on the 220 ring, west of the walkway, at (9.5, 220.5, -129.8) (band_wet_isolation.cpp:326-332; entity 2031, CarryKind::Load, 50 kg) and face north.
2. Action reads PICK UP / PIPE SPOOL (main_context.gd:345-351, name at :466-467). Tap it. The path is main.gd:909-910 request_pick_up, then bridge scraperx_simulation.cpp:200/699, then Simulation::request_pick_up (simulation.cpp:123-126), then commands.pick_up_requested (simulation.cpp:474), then PhysicsWorld::update_carry (physics_world_probes.cpp:502-508), then carry_candidate (:287-321), then attach_carry (:325-346), which adds a hands-to-spool point constraint.
3. Carry it east along the ring. The carrier is capped at 1.76 m/s (carry_speed_scale / carry_ground_acceleration, physics_world_probes.cpp:418-437); the swing is damped (:490-497) and the yaw held (:371-390).

designs.title: The chiller drop, rebuilt: drop into the shaft and get blown out of its mouth
designs.pitch:
The moment: at 256 m you push through E's steel door expecting a floor, and the floor isn't there. The cab is 2.85 m down an empty lift shaft. You step off the sill and fall. The blow of your landing lets go of a 5 t chiller somewhere above you. Through the shaft's sight glasses you see it plunge past the other way while its air drives the floor up under you at 3 m/s, twice today's speed. At 298 m the cab bursts out of the tube's mouth into open air, rides a skirt of roaring spray 1.7 m above the rim with nothing but sky around it, lifts your feet off the deck for a beat, and sinks back onto its own trapped air. It settles flush with F's platform.

The machine stays the same: a 5 t chiller falling in a sealed duct, with the air it pushes lifting a piston cab. That keeps the cascade, the ids and the start and end decks. What changes is everything the player touches and feels. Nothing is pulled and nothing is climbed. The start is your own fall. There is no governor, catch or dogs at the top: the cab is stopped by its own air spilling through a slotted collar at the shaft's mouth.

Why the cab sits 3 m lower: the drop is the act. The start deck the player stands on (D's platform at 256.25) and the end deck (298.25, beside F) are kept.
designs.what_the_player_does:
Touch only, and there is no Action press anywhere in this stage.

1. D parks at 256.25 as now, 0.25 m from E's door. The 140 kg hazard-painted leaf now stands shut but unlatched. Its hinge pins are set 0.1 rad out of plumb, so it falls shut on its own weight.
2. Push the stick south and walk into the door. It swings inward, into the shaft, under the body (about 125 N of push). Through the doorway there is no floor. The cab's landing deck lies 2.85 m below the sill, and the square of sky is 42 m overhead.
3. Keep walking off the sill and fall. A cautious player can instead turn their back and use DROP DOWN to lower into a hang from the sill, then let go (a fall of about 0.9 m). Either way works, and so does a jump on the spot once you are down. Standing or walking on the deck does nothing.
4. Ride, about 19 s. You can turn to watch the chiller through the west sight glasses, or the 264 and 286 rings sweep down through the east ones.
5. At the top the cab blows out of the mouth, floats and settles. Walk south off the deck, over the rim and the 0.4 m gap, onto F's platform at 298.25, as now.

The door shuts itself behind you about 1.5 s after you pass it. There is no link to perform. The door being shut is a physical condition the ride needs (see physics), and nothing the player grabs.
designs.what_they_feel_see_hear:
**Before.** D's arrival, then a heavy door that gives under the body. Beyond it is a dark steel shaft with hazard stripes on the sill's inner edge, a grated deck 3 m down, and far above a bright square of sky. Through 1.2 m armored sight glasses in the west wall, every 3 m from 258 to 296 m, the rust-and-galvanized chiller hangs at the top of its duct.

**The drop.**
- 0.8 s of fall, and the climber's own voice may yelp: that is a person, which is allowed.
- A hard landing (about 7.5 m/s, a pain grunt at most, far under the 20 m/s lethal speed).
- Under your feet the deck slams down 15 cm onto the cab's plate with a clang.
- Behind and above you the door booms shut.
- A sharp bang far overhead as the chiller's catch lets go, then a rising roar from under the floor as air is forced through the throttle.

**The launch.**
- 0.6 s after the blow the floor heaves. About 0.85 g of shove buckles the knees for half a second, then the cab runs steady at 3.05 m/s.
- The walls stream past, light grows, and the rings slide down outside the east glass.
- About 8 s in, at roughly 278 m, the 5 t block rushes down past the west glass an arm's length away, closing at about 6 m/s.

**The mouth.**
- At about 15.5 s the cab's skirt reaches the slotted collar (the shaft's top metre). Air screams out through the slots in sheets of spray all round the tube's mouth at your feet.
- The cab carries on up out of the tube: the deck peaks about 1.7 m above the rim, with the well open on every side.
- It decelerates faster than gravity (seal drag), so your feet leave the deck for about 0.2 s.
- It sinks back into the tube with the spray dying. The chiller lands far below with a deep thud, eased onto its stop.
- The cab bobs once on its trapped air and is still by about 19.5 s, flush beside F.

**Sound.** All machine sounds, no voices except the climber:
- a door slam, the deck clang, the catch bang;
- the throttle roar (band-passed noise rising with the duct's pressure);
- the collar blast (broadband hiss with the spill flow);
- the chiller's thud;
- the existing wet-band drips under it all.

**Haptics.** The existing load-scaled pulses on the landing, the launch shove and the settle.
designs.physics:
The causal chain. Every link is a body, a constraint or a declared force.

1. **The blow.** The landing deck (body 2045, reused) is a 60 kg steel grating, 2.5 m square, on its own vertical guide in the cab, as S1's plate is. A trip line runs from its north-east corner eye, over a sheave on a post above the shaft's north-east corner, to a 0.27 m crank on lever 2044, which is reshaped with a 157 kg counterweight at 0.35 m. The line holds the deck 0.15 m proud of the cab's top plate with up to 2.0 kN. A standing rider plus the deck is 1.42 kN, so weight alone never moves it. A falling body's momentum does: the rider at 7.5 m/s (635 N·s) meets about 409 kg of effective mass (rider, deck, and the lever's inertia reflected at the crank) and drives the deck the full 0.15 m onto the plate. That turns lever 2044 0.55 rad, past the chiller catch's existing 0.5 rad release.
2. **The release.** The chiller's catch (e_catch, unchanged, still keyed to lever 2044) unlatches. The 5 t chiller falls in its sealed duct and pushes its air through the throttle into the cab's cell.
3. **The lift.** The cab (2040) is a 900 kg steel box, 2.6 m square, whose sealing edge is its bottom, 1.75 m under its deck (a skirted piston). It feels (P − Patm) × 7.29 m² up. Seal drag is a constant 3 kN of guide friction (Kit::set_guide_friction, existing). There is no governor. The throttle (0.42 m²) sets the speed: about 6.3 kPa in the duct and about 1.74 kPa under the cab gives a steady 3.05 m/s.
4. **The door.** The leaf falls shut on its tilted hinge in about 1.5 s. Declared correction: a door now leaks and is pressed only while its opening lies under the piston's sealing edge (today it leaks wherever the cab is). The skirt reaches the sill about 2.4 s after the blow, by which time the door is shut. With the door shut, the cab's air presses the leaf onto its frame (it opens inward). A door wedged open makes the cab stall with its skirt at the doorway, spilling air through it: no seal, no lift.
5. **The stop.** Declared model: a vent collar. The shaft's top metre is slotted, 2.0 m² open per metre of height. Once the skirt's edge rises into it, the cell leaks the open slot area times the edge's height into the band. The cab overshoots out of the mouth, falls back as the spill drops the pressure, and recompresses its trapped air.
6. **The settle.** The chiller has about 6 m of travel beyond what the cab needs, so it keeps feeding air while the bounce dies. The bucket's governor eases the chiller onto its stop. When it lands, the cab sinks until the collar seals and stays on its trapped air, held there by seal friction. The existing bleed lowers it only about 1.5 cm/s.
7. **Re-arm (unchanged in kind).** The header's spout fills the bucket, which outweighs the chiller and hoists it 52.2 m back into its relatching catch. Its rise draws the cab's air, and the cab sinks to its rest (it outweighs the 3 kN seal drag). As the cab comes down, the deck's line goes taut again 0.15 m above the plate, so the deck is proud and armed again without the lever being thrown (60 kg arriving at 2 m/s moves it about 1 cm). The vacuum breaker stays on the cab's cell.

Rider: a moving support (rule 4). They stand on 2045, which rides on 2040. Deceleration at the top briefly exceeds g by the friction share, so the feet lift about 0.2 s; there is no hard landing.

Determinism (rule 10): no randomness or clocks. The final height is the deterministic product of the air budget and is pinned by test.

designs.rule_check:
**Rule 11 (no pull, no ladder).** Nothing in E is grabbed, pulled, hooked or pressed: the Action button offers nothing from D's deck to F's platform. The trip handle 2045 is gone (reused as the deck), the door is no longer carryable, and the latch 2043 is retired. No ladder, rung, pole or grid is added. The stage is "carried by something falling", started by a fall that the player's own momentum decides.

**Rule 9, checked against every machine and action on the route in the map:**
- **S1 scale plate (weight in a cage floor) and the slab incline's trip plate (weight on the trolley's deck).** E's deck holds 2.4 times a standing rider and ignores weight; only a fall drives it. The line-held tread is S1's kit part reused, which the rule allows; the encounter (stepping into an empty shaft and dropping onto the machine) is new.
- **S2's body shove, S3's pig into the pan, D's spool set in its gap, J's rail joint, the derrick's pigs.** Nothing is carried or set in E.
- **The swing's kick (a seated rider kicks a trip bar).** There is no trip within reach; the trigger is the whole body's fall.
- **The DROP into a hang in C4 and the AS-007 route.** Those are climbing moves. Here a drop starts a machine, and DROP DOWN is only the cautious variant.
- **C6's running leap.** That is horizontal, to a hold. E's is a deliberate fall into a shaft.
- **The hanging handle on E, F and G to O; rigging on A, B, F, G, I, K, M; N's flap chain.** All removed from E.
- **The slingshot (thrown by rubber).** E is not a throw: the rider rides a piston the whole way.
- **The vertical machines and the gondola (motor buttons), the tram (timing), the wheel (walking out on a plank), the trapeze, the zipline, the hook.** None is like it.

**The ride and arrival.** No other stage rides on air; old E, its only air ride, is replaced. D to L stop on governors, and M, N, O settle onto dogs. E has no governor, catch or dogs at the top: it blows out of its tube's mouth, floats on its own vented air and settles on its trapped air.

**New form and look.** A glazed pressure tube with a spraying slotted collar, and the drive (the chiller) seen through glass.

**Other rules.**
- Rule 1 (no link, no lift): stand at the brink as long as you like and nothing moves.
- Rule 3: the vent collar, the door's exposure and the seal friction are declared.
- Rule 5: a cab launched empty is re-armed by the cascade; otherwise the climbing route or the parachute. A rider who hang-drops still sets it off, so nobody is shut in the shaft.
- Rule 6 (built to be read): hazard sill, yellow rails, the line to the lever visible in the corner.
- Rule 10: deterministic.
- Machines make sounds; only the climber's own voice speaks.
designs.body_order_plan:
**No kit body is added, removed or split.** Every AS-007 body keeps its entity id, its kit index and its Jolt body id, in the same build order:
- 2040 cab: reshaped as a skirted box, placed 3 m lower, guide retuned.
- 2041 chiller: same parts, longer guide.
- 2042 door: heavier leaf, tilted hinge, carry flag removed, built shut.
- 2043 latch: built, then retired in place with kit.park() right after add_body, as D's add_retired does. Its lever and e_door_catch are kept, opened and set to never relatch, so the catch table keeps its size.
- 2044 lever: counterweight and crank reshaped, same pivot.
- 2045 handle: becomes the landing deck. New parts and mass, carry flag removed.
- 2046 bucket and 2047 striker: placed 7.2 m lower.

Static frame body 1005 changes only its parts: the shaft and duct walls run deeper, the rim is cut to 298.0, the slotted collar and the glazed panes are added, the basin moves, and a post with a sheave arm stands at the shaft's north-east corner. A part list is not a body list. Nothing touches world_solids.inc or solid_export.gd: kit bodies are not exported, so the 2026-10-20 failure path (a world solid shifting every later body) is not involved.

**Saved tables.** Catches (2), cells (2), ropes (1), bins (1), pools, reels and latches keep their counts. E's one trip line is re-laid (lever 2044 to the deck) rather than added; lines are not saved.

The one new constraint with saved state is the landing deck's vertical guide (one dog_floor entry). The comment follows the existing "so older saves line up" pattern. Every existing guide keeps its index. A save written before this grows by one guide and is refused by the size check, as with every earlier table growth. Bodies stay aligned.

The new kit behaviors carry no state: the vent collar, door exposure gating, and guide friction (existing API).

**Spawns.** No spawn is moved or added, so the keep-clear boxes that steer the zipline sweep and the tower's stock are unchanged. InitialSpawn::WetECab stays at (13.0, 257.2, -137.2). designs.risks:
1. **The blow may not reach the deck.** The player is a dynamic 85 kg capsule. If the movement code removes the vertical velocity on ground contact before the solver resolves it, the deck feels only weight. Measure the deck's travel on landing first. Fallback, declared: the native already knows each landing's impact speed (it scales landing sounds). Pass that momentum to the body landed on as an impulse, which is a general and truthful fix.
2. **The air numbers come from a lumped 2 kHz model; the kit steps at 90 Hz.** The 15 m³ cab cell is stiff at the start, so the launch shove, the overshoot and the final height may differ. Tune throttle, collar height, seal friction and excess chiller travel natively. The falsifiers pin the outcome (peak acceleration ≤ 12 m/s², settle within 25 s, flush within 0.1 m).
3. **The apex float.** Deceleration above g (seal drag) lifts the feet about 0.2 s. If it triggers airborne side-effects (a fear yelp, a landing stumble), lower the friction to about 1.5 kN or widen the collar.
4. **Conditional-builder drift.** The frame grows deeper and gains a post, so zipline or stock placement could change despite the hand check. The guard catches it; the remedy is the re-stage list.
5. **Saves.** One more saved guide means saves written before the change are refused (bodies still line up). Old saves would also restore E's old body states, which no longer fit the new geometry.
6. **The door.** A 140 kg self-closing leaf must not stall the walk and must shut before the skirt reaches the sill. Tune hinge tilt and damping. A wedged door makes the cab stall at the doorway; that is physical and recoverable by the bleed in about 2 minutes, but awkward.
7. **Empty launch.** A load dropped in (D's 50 kg spool) launches the cab empty. Recovery is the dump on TP-340, the climbing route, or the parachute. This is acceptable in a causal world.
8. **Spawn.** InitialSpawn::WetECab now launches E on load. Check whether any START option or other scenario spawns there expecting a still cab.
9. **Glass cost on the Fold.** Transparent overdraw from 26 or more panes: merge them and keep them few. The wet-band look must stay coherent.
10. **The bucket's longer 52.2 m hoist** may lengthen the re-arm past the band test's 150 s budget.
11. **Rule 9 reading.** The deck-on-a-line is S1's kit part. The defense is that weight never starts it and the encounter is the drop. The owner may still read it as "a plate again". If so, the trigger can become the cab's own dip on a counterweighted pit buffer, but its centimeter margins sit inside Jolt's contact slop.

designs.title: The man engine: climbing the wet shaft by stepping between two rocking rods (stage E, 256.25 to 298.25 m)
designs.pitch:
Stage E today is the chiller-drop cab. The rider shuts themselves into a 2.7 m steel box, pulls a spent hanging handle, and rides 28 s while a hidden 5 t chiller pushes air. This design replaces it with a water-driven double-rod man engine in the same shaft. The man engine is the Cornish mine machine that carried miners up and down a shaft on reciprocating rods.

How it works:
- Two steel rods, each 28.4 m long and 1.1 t, hang on one rope over two head sheaves, so they rock 7 m in opposition.
- Each rod carries three steps and an open bucket.
- The bucket at the top of its stroke fills under a roaring spout. Once its rod outweighs the other rod plus the rider, it sinks, and a striker at the bottom dumps it with a crash.

What the rider does:
- They climb 42 m in six strokes by stepping across a 14 cm gap, from the rod that has just risen to the rod that has just sunk.
- That is five transfers, in the engine's rhythm, with the other rod's steps rushing past 0.4 m from the shoulder.
- Nothing is pulled and nothing is climbed. The rider's own weight, put on the right rod at the right moment, decides every stroke. Stay where you are and the engine carries you back down.
- The float lift's arrival opens the engine's water, so the band stays a cascade.

What stays the same:
- The start and end decks: in through E's doorway at 256.25, out over the rim at 298.25 onto F's waiting platform.
- Every earlier body, zipline and stock spot. All new bodies are built after the whole world, after the Matron's throwables. The old cab, door, latch and trip handle are retired in their own slots.
designs.what_the_player_does:
Touch only. The stick does the work and the Action button stays blank, because nothing is pressed.

1. Ride the float lift (D) to 256.25 as today. In its last 0.25 m, D's deck lifts a bell crank on the outside of E's north wall, and the riser's main valve opens.
   - Water bursts into rod A's bucket 34 m up. Rod A sinks, and its first step (A1) comes down to the doorway sill about 6.5 s after D stops.
2. Walk south off D through the east part of E's doorway (x 13.1 to 13.6) onto the fixed landing in the shaft's east half (256.25).
3. When A1 settles level beside the landing, walk west about 1.3 m onto it.
   - Its stop clanks, and its bucket dumps with a crash onto a tray 26 m up.
4. Overhead, rod B's bucket fills. After a slow heave, A rises 7 m at up to 2 m/s. B's steps and dripping bucket rush down past you in the other half.
5. At the top, B's step settles level beside yours. Walk east onto it.
   - The steps come within the legs' 0.35 m step-up about 0.6 s before they stop, and the engine holds still about 1.6 s after. That is a window of about 2.2 s.
   - If you stay, your rod becomes the heavy side and carries you back down 7 m. You come up again about 9 s later and can try again.
6. Repeat, alternating west and east: A1 to B1 to A2 to B2 to A3 to B3. That is five transfers, about 55 s from stepping on A1.
7. On B3 at 298.25, level with the shaft's rim, walk south over the rim and the 0.4 m gap onto F's platform, exactly as today. The rest of the band is unchanged.

Other things the rider can do:
- Going down works the same way: step across at the bottom of your stroke.
- Stepping into the empty half drops you at most 2.25 m to the shaft floor at the bottom. A1 stops 2.15 m above the floor, so a rider there is never crushed.
- Higher up, the worst fall is about 14 m onto a lower step (16.6 m/s, under the 20 m/s lethal speed).
- With D down, the engine stands still.
designs.what_they_feel_see_hear:
What they see:
- A 2.7 m steel shaft, open to the sky 42 m up. Two yellow rods of chequer-plate steps rock against each other, with hazard nosing on their inner edges.
- Each rod carries a rust bucket in the strip along the north wall.
- Spouts roar into the top bucket. The bottom bucket opens on its striker and slams 465 kg of water onto a tray.
- Water sheets down the north wall and drips off every step.
- Two work lamps ride each rod, so light climbs and falls on the wet walls.
- Looking up: the headgear's two sheaves, the riser pipes, and the cistern hanging under TP-340, 36 m above.

What they feel:
- Each stroke starts with a slow, heavy heave while the falling bucket is still filling, then surges to 2 m/s.
- It eases onto its stop over the last 2 m with a deep clank, felt as a thud underfoot (haptics), plus a low rumble while rising.
- As you rise, the other rod's steps and its dripping bucket drop past at 4 m/s relative, 0.42 m from the body.
- At each top: a beat of stillness, the next step level beside you, a step across a 14 cm gap over 30-plus metres of shaft, and the engine heaves again.
- Missing a step is gentle and readable: you sink back 7 m and come up again.
- At 298 m you step out over the rim into daylight and wind onto F's platform. Below, the engine keeps working until its cistern runs dry.

What they hear (machines only, no voices):
- The spout's roar, rising as the bucket fills.
- The dump's crash and splatter.
- Rope creak over the sheaves and the scrape of the guide shoes.
- The stroke-end clank and the generic groan of the 1.1 t rods.
- The band's existing drips and the wet ambience.
designs.physics:
The mechanism uses only existing mechanism-kit parts, plus one build-time verb (`retire`).

1. **Coupling.** Rod A's head and rod B's head share one tension-only kit rope over two fixed head sheaves (ratio 1). The rods are equal (1,100 kg each), so they balance, and equal and opposite travel is enforced while the rope is taut.
   - Each rod has its own vertical guide with 7.0 m of travel.
   - The governor only ever opposes motion: it caps the speed at 2.0 m/s and eases into each stop.
   - Shoe friction is 600 N per guide.
   - The rope and the guide stops carry the load at each end.
2. **Drive: water only, in a declared model.**
   - Each rod's bucket is a kit water bin. Its first part is the bucket floor, and its contents add to the rod's mass.
   - Two spouts are fed from a 30 t cistern under TP-340 by kit pipes, with Q = 0.6 A √(2 g Δh).
   - Each spout pipe has two gates:
     - (a) The main valve. Its lever is a bell crank lifted by D's deck at the top of D's travel: a contact link.
     - (b) The bucket's own seat. Declared model: the bucket's lip holds the spout's flap open only while its rod is within 1.5 m of the top of its stroke (set_pipe_spool with the rod as the seated body).
   - The stream passes straight down into that bucket.
3. **Reversal.**
   - The top bucket fills until its side outweighs the other side plus friction:
     (m_rod + w_top) − (m_rod + w_bottom_left + rider on the other rod) > 2F/g = 122 kg.
   - It then sinks. It keeps filling over its first 1.5 m, so the drive builds from near zero. That is the slow heave, followed by the governed surge.
   - At the bottom, its floor turns a striker (a kit lever). The bin's gate opens, and the bucket dumps at 220 kg/s onto a static tray, where the water drains.
4. **The rider's weight is part of the balance.**
   - On the rod that has just risen, the rider's 85 kg makes it the heavy side as soon as the other bucket has dumped enough, so it carries them back down.
   - Stepping across to the rod that has just sunk makes that side heavier, and the next stroke lifts them.
   - Steady state:
     - Dwell with the rider across ≈ (85 + 122) / Q.
     - Time until a rider who stays starts back down ≈ (W − 85 + 122) / (Q + R), where W is the water in the bucket on arrival.
   - Stability, so water never piles up in the buckets: R ≥ Q + Q²·t_gate / (85 + 2F/g).
5. **Rule 1: no link, no lift.** With D down, the main valve is shut. No water flows and nothing moves. With D up, the engine runs whether or not anyone is aboard, until the cistern is empty.
6. **Rule 2: energy pays for height.**
   - Each tick: released = Σ over both bins of (contents × g × the rod's descent). The rods' own masses cancel because they are equal and opposite.
   - The rider's gain must stay ≤ released.
   - The cistern's water loses about 40 m of head in the pipe, which is not counted, so the bound is conservative.
7. **Re-arm.** The header's dump on TP-340 refills the cistern through a fourth riser branch, valved by the existing dump bar like D's tank branch. Lowering D shuts the main valve: the engine finishes its stroke and stops.
8. **Declared simplifications** for the stage record: massless rope; streams carry no momentum; buckets dump at a fixed rate; the spout's flap is the seat gate above.

designs.rule_check:
**Rule 11: no pull, no ladder.**
- No pull:
  - E's grab targets (door 2042, door latch 2043, chiller trip handle 2045) are retired.
  - The engine has nothing to take hold of.
  - Its only inputs are D's arrival (contact on the bell crank) and the rider's weight.

  - CLIMB is never offered or used. The rods' steps are ridden platforms 14 m apart on each rod, never climbed hand over hand.
  - The rule-8 backup (AS-007's climbing route, body 1006) is untouched.

**Rule 9: no repeat.** Checked against every machine and act in the map.
- S1, weight on a scale plate (a water-balance hoist). E shares S1's drive physics: a bucket filling at the head. It does not share the act. There is no plate, the start is D's arrival, and the act is the transfer. The kit's parts are reused freely; the encounter is not.
- S2 (shoving with the body), S3 (pig set in the pan), D (spool carried and laid in its gap), J (rail joint laid), G-H (tail pin carried out): E has no carrying, placing, removing or shoving.
- Shackle rigging and hooking: AS-006 A/B, F, G, I, K and M. E has no rigging.
- The spent hanging handle (E and F today; G to M and O): none.
- N and O (gravel into a hopper or bucket drives a cab): the rider stands still in a cage. Here the rider moves between two machines.
- Slingshot (launch), the swing and K (pendulums), trapeze and pipe gallery (swinging by hand), ziplines: none.
- Stone wheel (walk out on a plank, ride a bucket over the top), slab incline (trip plate, brake treadle), derrick (throwing pigs off), crown gondola, cascade mast, pitman lift (hauling a line), barrel helix: different acts and forms.
- **Nearest neighbor: the traction tram.** The tram turns on timing (a shuttle that waits 6 s and 4 s, and a miss carries you back down). The engine is also about timing, and also returns a late rider downward. But its act is a repeated step from one moving platform to another, five times in rhythm between counter-moving rods, not boarding one shuttle once. This should be put to the owner.
- **New and named:**
  - Action: "step across", moving your weight onto the rod that has just sunk.
  - Form: counter-reciprocating step rods, which no stage has.
  - Look: a wet, lamp-lit, roaring shaft with water buckets riding the rods.

- Rule 1 (no link, no lift): with D down, nothing moves.
- Rule 2 (energy pays for height): the per-tick ledger above.

designs.risks:
1. **The transfer window on a phone.** About 2.2 s is the target, from a hand model.
   - Water-balance timing is sensitive to Q, R, the shoe friction F and the 1.5 m gate. Too slow a dump piles water in the buckets, and then the window collapses to about 0.3 s.
   - Mitigation: the stability rule R ≥ Q + Q²·t_gate/(85 + 2F/g), and a native assertion over 20 cycles.
   - Tune with F or Q, never with a timer. A miss only costs about 18 s.
2. **The player controller between two dynamic supports.**
   - A rider half across when the rods start can take a support jolt and stumble (kSupportJoltMargin).
   - A rider hugging an inner edge or standing in the doorway can be clipped by a passing step: at most 4 m/s, under the 6 m/s at which a blow is felt, so a shove, not a death.

4. **Kit::retire is new.**

designs.title: The chiller drop at 256 m becomes a glass air tube: walk in, knock the trip bob off the crosshead with a thrown flange, and ride the chiller's air while it falls past you
designs.pitch:
The machine stays as it is: a 5 t chiller falls 45 m in a sealed duct, and the air it pushes lifts a cab 42 m, from 256.25 m (beside D's top) to 298.25 m (beside F). The handle and the door drag go. Three things change: the start, what the rider can see, and what they hear.

- **The walls are glass.** The cab tube and the duct's east and north faces are drawn as wet wired glass. Only the material changes; no shape does.
- **The door shuts itself.** It is a plug door on a leaning (rising-butt) hinge. The rider pushes it open by walking in, and its own weight swings it shut behind them. The air pressure then holds it on its frame, so it needs no latch.
- **The start is a throw.** A yellow crosshead stands 3 m over the cab floor, and a hazard-striped 10 kg iron bob sits in a saddle on it. From the bob, the chiller's trip line rises 39 m to the tube's rim and on to the trip lever over the duct. The rider picks up one of three 12 kg cast-iron blind flanges lying in the cab and looks up; the throw arc shows the path. THROW: the flange tumbles up and clangs off the bob, which drops out of its saddle and snaps its slack line taut. Forty-seven meters up, the lever kicks over and the catch lets go with a bang.
- **The ride.** The chiller drops onto its own air with a whump the rider feels in the floor. The crossover under their feet roars, and the cab rises at 3 m/s. At about 277 m the chiller passes the other way, a meter beyond two panes of glass: a galvanized block the size of a car, closing at 6 m/s.

The throw has never started a stage on this route. Nothing is grabbed or pulled, and there is no ladder.
designs.what_the_player_does:
Touch only. The start (256.25 m) and the end (298.25 m) stay where they are.

1. **Arrive.** The rider rides D's float platform to 256.25 m, which stops 0.25 m from E's door as now. With the stick, they walk south into the door. It opens inward, so the body pushes the 60 kg leaf aside.
2. **The door shuts behind them.** Inside the 2.7 m glass box, the leaf swings to on its own in about 2.5 s and closes with a soft thud. There is no Action and no latch.
3. **Pick up a flange.** Three cast-iron blind flanges (12 kg, 0.46 m across) lie in the cab's south-west corner. Facing one, Action reads PICK UP; tap it. Both hands hold the flange, and the Jump button now reads THROW.
4. **Aim.** Drag-look up at the bob on the crosshead, 3.1 m over the deck. The throw arc (throw_arc_view.gd) shows the flange falling short when the reticle is on the bob. The rider learns to look a hand's width above it, along the yellow line. The shot works from 1.5 to 2.1 m off the bob's plumb, at 60 to 69 degrees.
5. **Throw.** Tap THROW. On a hit, the bob tips out of its saddle and the catch lets go within about a second. On a miss, the flange falls back into the tube: pick it up and throw again. Nothing is lost, because the tube is closed on all four sides and a throw rises at most 2.2 m above the hands.
6. **Ride.** The cab rises about 17 s to its stop, flush with the rim. The rider walks south over the rim onto F's platform, as now.

Other ways it can go, all caused by the physics:

- **Door held open.** A rider who stands in the doorway, holding the leaf open with their body, and throws from there sends the chiller down with the air pouring out of the doorway. The cab stays down, and E is spent until the header dump on TP-340 re-arms it. This is the stage's "no link, no lift" case.
- **No Action ever reads GRAB in the cab.**
- **Re-ride after a re-arm.** The bob hangs about 1.9 m above the floor below its saddle. A flange thrown up into it lifts it, and its fall back jerks the line again. Nothing can be grabbed.
designs.physics:
Everything uses the kit's declared models (AS-007). E's machine chain is unchanged: duct cell, cab cell, throttle, breaker, bleed, chiller, catch, hoist bucket, rope and striker.

1. **The door: a plug door that closes by its own weight.** It keeps its body (2042) and its hinge (e_door_hinge).
   - The hinge axis leans 6 degrees out of plumb, to (0, cos 6°, sin 6°), so the leaf rises as it swings in. A rising-butt hinge is a real fitting.
   - Its weight gives a closing torque of m·g·r·sin6°·cosθ: 34 N·m when shut and 9 N·m at 1.3 rad. The body pushes it open by contact, the same physics S2's bolt and the shoved stock use.
   - The door opens inward, so the existing door model presses it onto its frame once the cell has pressure. As before, an open door leaks its area times its opening.
   - The spring latch is no longer used. The door catch is built with relatch false and left open, so the latch body (2043) is a plain part.
2. **The knock.** A thrown flange is ordinary loose stock with the throw's real velocity. Its hit on the bob is a Jolt contact. The bob is a dynamic body sitting in a shallow saddle (2 to 3 cm lips) on the cab's crosshead.
3. **The trip.** The bob is the lower end of E's existing trip line. It is laid with 1.2 m of slack, so the knocked-off bob falls freely before the line takes it up.
   - The line is a pulley constraint, tension only, the existing add_trip_line. It runs from the bob, up over sheave 2 on the tube's north rim, across over sheave 1 above the duct, to the eye of the trip lever (2044).
   - The bob's jerk turns the counterweighted lever past 0.5 rad. The catch loop in Kit::pre_step unlatches the chiller, unchanged.
   - The lever then returns on its own counterweight: 115 N·m against the hanging bob's 98 N·m. So the catch can relatch when the header dump hoists the chiller back.
4. **The drive.** Unchanged, except for two numbers:
   - the chiller falls in its duct cell, and the air goes through the crossover throttle into the cab cell, now 0.4 m² instead of 0.2 m²;
   - the cab's governor caps the cab at 3.0 m/s with 40 kN, instead of 2.0 m/s with 25 kN, and still eases it to its stop at 1 m/s².
5. **The ride.** As every ride is, the cab is a moving support under the rider (rule 4).
6. **After the ride.** As the cab rises, the line goes slack because sheave 2 is above, and the bob settles on the cab floor. When a re-arm lowers the cab, the line takes the bob up again, and it hangs about 1.2 m below its saddle with the lever at rest.

designs.rule_check:
**Rule 11 (no pull, no ladder)**
- No handle, lanyard or Handle-kind carry is left in the stage.
- The door is pushed open by walking and shuts by its own weight.
- The bob is struck, never held.
- The lever turns by the bob's own fall.
- No ladder: the crosshead posts are 0.12 m box sections. The native test asserts that the climb probe never offers CLIMB on them.
- The experience is one rule 11 names, "carried by something falling", and the falling chiller is now seen.

**Rule 9, against every action on the route** (from the map). None of these starts a stage with a throw:
- S1: stand on a scale plate.
- S2: shove a shoot bolt with the body.
- S3: carry a pig into the pan on its trip line.
- C1–C3: ladders and leaps.
- AS-006 A and B: UNHOOK/HOOK and GRAB. C: a pulled rebar.
- AS-012 swing: kick the trip, ride the seat. C6: running leap and balance.
- D: carry the spool into its gap.
- F: HOOK the hose, pull the stop-valve handle.
- G, I, K, M: rig a rope, pull a lanyard. H: tail pin carried, then a lanyard. J: rail joint carried, then a lanyard.
- L: two pulls. N: GRAB the flap chain. O: a lanyard.
- C4/C5 and the AS-007 route: climbs.
- Crown gondola: vault aboard. Derrick: drop pigs to lighten it.
- Slingshot: draw and release the bands. Trapeze: catch and pump. Zipline. Hook: fire and winch. Pitman: haul by hand. Mast and helix: RAISE/CALL. Stone wheel: reload the hopper.
- Forklift and yard crane: driven. Matron: knock her down and throw at her.

**New here**
- An aimed throw straight up to knock a trip off its perch.
- A door that closes itself.
- A glass tube with the counterweight seen passing.

**Honest overlaps**
1. A weight on a trip line is the same kit idea as S3's pan. The encounters differ: S3 is carry and let go into a pan; here a bob is knocked off a perch overhead by a throw. If the owner reads it as S3 again, the fallback is to give the bob no weight of its own role and have it turn the lever by the flange's impulse alone. That is weaker physics.
2. THROW is the Matron's verb. It is reused as a verb, not as an encounter.
3. PICK UP is shared, but here it is only how the flange gets into the hands.

**Other rules**
- Rule 1 (no link, no lift): the door held open means the cab stays down.
- Rule 2: gain ≤ released is checked every tick.
- Rule 3: contact, constraints and the declared air model.
- Rule 6: the bob and the line are marked yellow/hazard, and the line is drawn all the way.
- Rule 10: deterministic; no random input.
- Rule 5: after a misfire, the cascade re-arms E, or the rider takes the climbing route, the swing and C6 alternative, or the parachute.

designs.risks:
1. **The door.** It must open under a walking body and close itself reliably, without bouncing back off its frame or jamming against the rider. Tune the lean (4–8°), the leaf's damping and the seal. The door-open falsifier also proves that a door left ajar is safe.
2. **The shot's difficulty.** At the 7 m/s cap and 1.2 rad pitch cap, the bob at 3.1 m needs a steep aim, and looking straight at it falls short. The arc preview teaches this. If touch players struggle, lower the crosshead to 2.8 m: the beam still blocks a jump's head from bumping the bob. Verify on the Fold, where nothing has been measured yet.
3. **The knock and the jerk** are contact- and solver-sensitive. Log the lever's peak angle and the bob's unseating natively. If the 47 J margin proves thin, add slack (1.2 → 1.5 m) or weight (10 → 11 kg, still under 115 N·m).
4. **Strike-backs.** A flange falling back, or the dangling bob, can strike the rider: about 8 m/s at most, under the arm-break speed. Verify there is no lethal or arm-break event in the test.
5. **The posts as poles.** If the climb probe treats the crosshead posts as poles, a rider could climb to the bob and shove it. That is acceptable as physics but must not count as a ladder; the test asserts no CLIMB offer, else widen the posts to 0.2 m.
6. **Faster ride.** 3 m/s and a 0.4 m² throttle change E's timing in touch_wet and touch_stack (shorter by about 11 s). The re-arm's air path also changes; the band re-arm check covers it.
7. **Index arithmetic.** It spreads over the Matron's list, holding_throwable and four test sites. Missing one silently mis-indexes stock.
8. **The Matron and the flanges.** As a pest she takes light stock up to 25 kg. If her deck-to-deck roaming reaches 256 m she could carry the flanges off. Any piece of 12 kg or less the rider brings still works.
9. **Re-ride after a re-arm** depends on a throw from below lifting the dangling bob; this is not covered by a test. Add a native check, or name it out of scope.
10. **Glass on the phone:** transparency sorting and draw calls on the Fold, measured nowhere. Keep the glass to E's nine parts.
11. **Rule 9 reading.** The owner may read the bob on the trip line as S3's pan again (see rule_check). The fallback is noted there.
12. **Saves.** Older saves load, since the bodies are appended and the tables are unchanged. But a save made mid-E under the old design holds the door open at 0.9 rad and the handle at its old pose. scores.why:
Strongest moment of the three. You step off a sill into an empty shaft, the landing sets off the launch, the cab shoves you up at about 0.85 g, the chiller rushes past behind glass, and the cab blows out of the tube's mouth with a moment of float. The only input is walking: no button, no aiming, nothing to read.

Checked against the code:
- It is the only design that saw the real speed limit. The hoist bucket's guide governs the chiller through a 1:1 rope at 2.0 m/s and 25 kN (band_wet_isolation.cpp:453), and design 1 raises it to 4.0 m/s. Without that, no cab goes faster than about 2 m/s.
- Today's door leaks wherever the cab is (mechanism_kit.cpp:1242-1245), even though the doorway sits above the piston at the start. Design 1 names this as a fault and fixes it with a doorway-exposure rule.
- The vent collar is a declared model.
- The blow numbers check out: 635 N·s into about 409 kg is about 496 J, against 87 J of spare hold. The player is a plain dynamic Jolt body and nothing in src/sim scales contact mass, so the contact solver should carry the momentum.
- No body is added or removed. One guide is added at the end, and it correctly says this makes older saves fail to load (dog_floor is read at exact size, physics_world_state.cpp:373).
- The WetECab spawn is used only by tests (sim_tests_wet.cpp:196, 206), so its risk 8 is harmless.
- The world guard plus the named re-stage list is the right answer to the body-order lesson.

Weak points:
- The landing deck is S1's scale plate almost exactly: a tread on its own vertical guide, held proud of the floor by a line from its north-east corner eye to a lever crank (band_stack.cpp:495-507). Only the tuning differs: a blow starts it, weight does not.
- Only 0.05 rad separates the catch's release (0.5) from the deck bottoming (0.55), which is about 1.4 cm of deck.
- Latch 2043 is parked before its add_lever. That puts a hinge on a body that is out of the physics world.
- At the top the cab is held only by friction. The ±3 kN seal friction is about ±410 Pa, so the final height spreads about ±0.2 m against a 0.1 m test. After about 12 s the bleed lets the cab creep down at about 1.5 cm/s.
- If the fallback is needed (passing landing momentum on as an impulse), that is a change to shared player physics. It touches S1's plate and the slab incline's trip plate, and needs the full suite, not only the AS-007 groups.

The most honest physics: the rider's own 85 kg is part of the water balance on every stroke. A wet, lamp-lit man engine with counter-moving rods is a real and unique sight.

It only works if a 2.2 s transfer window, taken from a hand model, holds up. Five timed steps across a gap with a floating stick on a phone, each miss costing about 18 s, risks being a chore rather than being swept up in the climb.

Rules:
- Its drive is S1's water balance yet again: a bucket filling at the head, as in S1, and as N and O drive with a filling bucket.
- Its act (catch the moment, or be carried back down) is the traction tram's. It flags both itself.
- Stepping up a shaft on moving steps reads as a ladder with timing under rule 11's spirit (*"fucking ladders"*).

Buildability, checked against the code:
- It says older saves will load once rope_anchor, rope_parted and pool_water are read with list_up_to. But it adds two guides, and dog_floor is read at exact size (physics_world_state.cpp:373), so older saves are still refused.
- It needs a new Kit::retire (pulling sliders, pistons and lines off parked bodies, and changing restore), six late bodies that the zipline sweep and stock dressing never saw (headgear, riser, a 30 t cistern under TP-340), and native tuning of the water balance.
- The whole old chiller drop stays as dead scenery, and the header's old bucket branch still pours into it.
- Appending bodies after the Matron's throwables is a sound way to keep the order.

The chain is all real: a thrown flange hits the bob by contact, the bob falls, its slack line takes up and jerks the lever. The rising-butt hinge math is right (m·g·r·sin6°·cosθ, about 34 N·m).

But it gets its own headline number wrong. It raises the throttle and the cab's governor but leaves the hoist bucket's 2.0 m/s, 25 kN governor (band_wet_isolation.cpp:453). Through the 1:1 rope that caps the chiller, and so the cab, at about 2 m/s, so the claimed 17 s ride at 3 m/s cannot happen as specified.

Its claim that every reshaped part stays inside the tube (256 to 259.45 m) misses the travel envelope. The zipline sweep sees kit travel envelopes, and the crosshead raises the cab's swept top to about 301.4 m, above the 298.2 rim.

The throw checks out against the code (7 m/s cap, pitch clamped at 1.2 rad, physics_world_probes.cpp:576). But a 60 to 69 degree lob from 1.5 to 2.1 m off the bob's plumb can only be thrown from a corner of a 2.6 m box, and a 12 kg iron flange can fall back onto the thrower.

Rules:
- The trigger is a weight on a string that trips the lever. After a re-arm the bob literally hangs on its line, which is the owner's own picture of the spent encounter: *"a block hanging from a string"*.
- THROW is the Matron's verb, and S3's pan is the nearest neighbor.

It also spends work on the Matron: index-accessor rework in her throwables list, in holding_throwable, and in four test sites including sim_tests_matron.cpp. As a pest she takes stock of 25 kg or less (the 12 kg flanges included). That runs against the user's latest word to stop spending on her.

The ride itself is today's E behind glass. Cheapest to build: bodies are only appended, and no saved table changes.

verdict.grafts:
Into the winner:

1. **The door, from design 3.** Use its leaned (rising-butt) hinge on a lighter leaf: 60 to 80 kg at a 6 to 8 degree lean, about 34 to 45 N·m when shut and a 35 to 60 N push. This replaces the 140 kg leaf on a 0.1 rad tilt, so a walking body opens it easily. Re-check that it still shuts within about 1.5 s, before the skirt reaches the sill. Also take design 3's falsifier "door held open, the machine is spent, the chiller runs out" as the winner's wedged-door case.

2. **The glass, from design 3.** Make it a material on a few existing wall spans: the shaft's west face and the duct's east face, split into a handful of spans. Drop the 26-plus separate panes. Fewer transparent draws on the Fold, and a smaller change to frame 1005, which the zipline sweep sees.

3. **Life in the shaft, from design 2.**
   - Presentation-only work lamps parented to the cab, so light climbs the wet walls during the 15 s run.
   - Drip emitters off the deck while it moves.
   - A haptic rumble while the cab moves, on top of the launch and settle pulses.
   - Its native check that no built zipline's cable room or footing, and no stock piece, overlaps any changed body or travel envelope. Add it to the winner's count-and-order guard.
   - Its save test: a save cut to the old table sizes either loads or is refused cleanly, and parked bodies stay parked after a death restore.

4. **Fixes to the winner itself:**
   - Widen the trigger margin: crank about 0.25 m, so the deck bottoms near 0.6 rad against the catch's 0.5 rad release, instead of 0.55 against 0.5.
   - Retire latch 2043 without parking it before its hinge is built. Leave it built, inert and not carryable, or park it after its lever and catch are made.
   - Pin the friction-held top height with a test of the rider walking off at 30 s, and size the bleed against the 0.35 m step-up.
   - Measure the blow on the real contact solver first. If the landing-impulse fallback is needed, treat it as a shared-physics change: it reaches S1's plate and the slab incline's trip plate, so run the full native suite, not only the AS-007 groups.
verdict.rule_violations:
None of the three breaks rule 11 outright: none adds a pull-started lift or a ladder on the route. Named exposures:

**Rule 9, design 3 (closest to a violation).** Its trigger is a weighted bob on a trip line that turns the chiller's lever. After a re-arm the bob hangs from its line about 1.9 m over the floor, and a re-ride means throwing at it. That is the owner's own 2026-09-30 picture of the spent encounter: *"You walk up to a block hanging from a string"*. Only the verb has changed, and that verb (THROW) is the Matron's. It also touches the Matron's code and tests, against the user's 2026-10-20 *"enough work on the matron"*.

**Rule 9, design 2.**
- Its act (be at the right place at the right moment, or be carried back down) repeats the traction tram's timing shuttle.
- Its drive (a bucket filling at the head) is S1's water balance again, and N and O also drive with a filling bucket.
- It reads as a moving ladder under rule 11's spirit.
- It flags the first two itself. All three are for the owner to rule on.

**Rule 9, design 1 (the winner).** Its landing deck reuses S1's scale plate as a part: a tread on its own guide, on a line from its north-east corner eye to a lever crank (band_stack.cpp:495-507). Reusing kit parts is allowed, and the encounter (a fall into a shaft) is new. Put it to the owner as the one open question.

**Factual errors that a rule check depends on:**
- **Design 3's ride speed.** Its 3 m/s ride is impossible with the bucket's 2.0 m/s governor left as it is (band_wet_isolation.cpp:453).
- **Design 3's "inside the tube" claim.** The crosshead raises the cab's travel envelope above the rim, so the body-order claim needs its own zipline guard.
- **Design 2's save claim.** It says older saves will load, but its two new guides make dog_floor's exact-size read refuse them (physics_world_state.cpp:373).

**Process (2026-10-20 directive, not a rule-book breach).** Each new experience is talked through and refined with the owner before it is built. The winner goes to the owner as a design, not straight into code.
